concepts.name: Levels of body organization
concepts.summary: Name the levels from cells to tissues, organs, organ systems and the whole organism, and give an example of each.

concepts.name: Major organ systems and roles
concepts.summary: Describe in one sentence the main job of each major organ system, such as circulatory, respiratory, digestive, skeletal and nervous.

concepts.name: Skeleton and joints
concepts.summary: Identify major bones and joint types and explain that the skeleton supports, protects and allows movement.

concepts.name: Muscle types and movement
concepts.summary: Distinguish skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscle and explain how muscles pull on bones to move the body.

concepts.name: Heart and blood circuit
concepts.summary: Explain that the heart pumps blood through arteries, capillaries and veins to deliver oxygen and nutrients and carry away wastes.

concepts.name: Breathing and gas exchange
concepts.summary: Trace air from nose to alveoli and explain that oxygen enters the blood while carbon dioxide leaves.

concepts.name: Digestive tract path
concepts.summary: List the organs food passes through from mouth to anus and state what each mainly does.

concepts.name: Homeostasis as stable internal conditions
concepts.summary: Explain that the body keeps conditions such as temperature and blood sugar within a narrow range.

misconceptions.text: Air we breathe goes into the stomach or directly into the blood as whole breaths.
Veins always carry deoxygenated blood and arteries always carry oxygenated blood.
Muscles can push bones as well as pull them.

concepts.name: Heart chambers and valves
concepts.summary: Describe the four chambers, the valves and the pulmonary and systemic circuits and follow blood through them.

concepts.name: Blood components and functions
concepts.summary: Relate red cells, white cells, platelets and plasma to oxygen transport, defence and clotting.

concepts.name: Ventilation mechanics
concepts.summary: Apply the roles of the diaphragm, intercostal muscles and pressure changes to explain inhalation and exhalation.

concepts.name: Digestion and absorption sites
concepts.summary: Match enzymes and organs (salivary glands, stomach, pancreas, liver, small intestine) to the nutrients they break down and where absorption occurs.

concepts.name: Nephron filtration and urine formation
concepts.summary: Outline how kidneys filter blood, reabsorb useful substances and excrete urea and excess water as urine.

concepts.name: Skin layers and functions
concepts.summary: Name epidermis, dermis and hypodermis and link them to protection, sensation and temperature control.

concepts.name: Nervous and endocrine signalling
concepts.summary: Contrast fast electrical nerve signals with slower hormonal signals carried in blood, using examples.

concepts.name: Simple negative feedback loops
concepts.summary: Apply the sensor, control centre and effector pattern to examples such as body temperature.

misconceptions.text: Most digestion and nutrient absorption happens in the stomach.
The right side of the heart carries blood to the body and the left side to the lungs.
Lungs inflate themselves by actively pulling in air with their own muscle.

concepts.name: Cardiac cycle and conduction
concepts.summary: Explain systole, diastole, valve action and the SA node to AV node to Purkinje conduction sequence and link them to an ECG.

concepts.name: Blood pressure regulation
concepts.summary: Analyse how cardiac output, vessel resistance and baroreceptor reflexes determine blood pressure.

concepts.name: Gas transport and oxygen dissociation
concepts.summary: Analyse how hemoglobin loads and unloads oxygen and how CO2 is carried, including effects of pH and temperature.

concepts.name: Muscle contraction mechanism
concepts.summary: Explain sliding filaments, calcium and ATP use, and the neuromuscular junction in contraction.

concepts.name: Hormone axes and glands
concepts.summary: Analyse hypothalamus-pituitary-target gland axes and the actions of insulin, glucagon, thyroid hormones and cortisol.

concepts.name: Nephron transport and fluid balance
concepts.summary: Analyse filtration, reabsorption and secretion along the nephron and how ADH and aldosterone adjust urine.

concepts.name: Innate and adaptive immunity
concepts.summary: Compare nonspecific defences with B and T cell responses, antibodies and immune memory, and the role of lymph nodes.

concepts.name: Reproductive systems and cycles
concepts.summary: Describe male and female reproductive anatomy and apply hormonal control of gametogenesis, ovulation and the menstrual cycle.

misconceptions.text: Hormones act on every cell, so target specificity does not matter.
Antibiotics strengthen the immune system and work against viruses.
Muscle contraction shortens the filaments themselves.

concepts.name: Integrated cardiovascular-renal control
concepts.summary: Analyse how the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, ADH and the heart together defend blood pressure and volume.

concepts.name: Acid-base balance mechanisms
concepts.summary: Analyse how buffers, respiration and the kidneys together hold blood pH near 7.4 and interpret respiratory versus metabolic disturbances.

concepts.name: Exercise and stress responses
concepts.summary: Analyse how sympathetic activation and hormones redistribute blood flow, ventilation and metabolism during exercise and stress.

concepts.name: Glucose and energy homeostasis
concepts.summary: Evaluate how insulin, glucagon and the liver regulate blood glucose and judge what goes wrong in type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

concepts.name: Positive feedback and feedforward control
concepts.summary: Distinguish positive feedback in childbirth and clotting from negative feedback and explain anticipatory control.

concepts.name: Pathophysiology from organ dysfunction
concepts.summary: Evaluate how failure in one organ, such as heart failure or kidney disease, cascades to other systems.

concepts.name: Immune dysregulation and tolerance
concepts.summary: Evaluate how loss of self-tolerance or overreaction produces autoimmunity, allergy and immunodeficiency.

concepts.name: Interpreting physiological measurements
concepts.summary: Interpret ECG, spirometry, blood gases and urinalysis to infer the state of organ systems.

misconceptions.text: Homeostasis means variables are held constant rather than regulated around a set point with fluctuations.
Type 2 diabetes is simply a lack of insulin, same as type 1.
Positive feedback is always harmful to the body.

concepts.name: Systems-level modelling of regulation
concepts.summary: Build models of multi-organ regulation including gain, delay and oscillation and predict responses to perturbation.

concepts.name: Evaluating physiological evidence
concepts.summary: Judge the quality of human and animal physiology studies, including limits of extrapolating across species and populations.

concepts.name: Variation across age and sex
concepts.summary: Evaluate how development, ageing, pregnancy and sex differences alter normal ranges and regulatory set points.

concepts.name: Adaptation and acclimatization
concepts.summary: Evaluate short and long-term adaptations to altitude, heat, training and disuse and distinguish their mechanisms.

concepts.name: Multi-system differential reasoning
concepts.summary: Weigh competing physiological explanations for a complex presentation across several organ systems and justify the most likely.

concepts.name: Designing physiological interventions
concepts.summary: Design interventions or experiments that target a feedback loop and anticipate compensatory responses and side effects.

concepts.name: Teaching integrated physiology
concepts.summary: Create coherent explanations and teaching models that connect structure, mechanism and regulation across systems.

misconceptions.text: Normal reference ranges apply identically to all people regardless of age, sex or conditions.
Animal model results transfer directly to humans.
Correcting one abnormal variable with a treatment has no knock-on effects because feedback loops are independent.
